content:
# Sirach 26 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 26 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 13

---

## Disagreement 001 — 26:3 "good portion / precious gift / given in the lot"
**Verse:** 26:3
**EMET:** "A-good-wife is a-good-portion; she-will-be-given in-the-portion of-those-who-fear"
**LOGOS:** "A good wife is a good portion; she is given in the lot of those who fear the LORD"
**PNEUMA:** "A good wife is a precious gift; she is given to those who fear the LORD"
**Issue:** μερίς — "portion/lot/share." EMET and LOGOS both use "portion" twice (capturing the repetition). PNEUMA substitutes "precious gift" for the first "portion," losing the lot/allocation metaphor which has covenantal resonance.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A good wife is a good portion; she is given in the lot of those who fear the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 002 — 26:5 "my-heart was-in-dread / fear / tremble"
**Verse:** 26:5
**EMET:** "my-heart was-in-dread"
**LOGOS:** "caused my heart to fear"
**PNEUMA:** "made my heart tremble"
**Issue:** ἐφοβήθη ἡ καρδία μου — "my heart feared." EMET's "was-in-dread" is vivid; LOGOS is direct; PNEUMA's "tremble" is more physical. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Three things caused my heart to fear."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 26:6 "jealous of another-wife / jealous of a rival wife / jealous of a rival"
**Verse:** 26:6
**EMET:** "a-wife who-is-jealous of another-wife"
**LOGOS:** "a wife jealous of a rival wife"
**PNEUMA:** "a wife who is jealous of a rival"
**Issue:** ζήλῳ γυναικός — "jealousy of a woman." The context implies a co-wife situation (polygyny). EMET and LOGOS preserve "another wife/rival wife." SOPHIA uses "who rivals another" to capture the rivalry without inserting "wife" twice.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a jealous wife who rivals another."

---

## Disagreement 004 — 26:9 "fornication / unchastity" and eye-lifting
**Verse:** 26:9
**EMET:** "The-fornication of a-woman is in-the-lifting of-her-eyes"
**LOGOS:** "The unchastity of a woman shows in the way she lifts her eyes"
**PNEUMA:** "An unchaste woman advertises herself in how she looks around"
**Issue:** πορνεία — "fornication/prostitution/sexual immorality." EMET preserves the strong term; LOGOS softens to "unchastity"; PNEUMA paraphrases further. The Greek is direct: her porneia is visible in her eyes. SOPHIA uses "unchastity" as a middle ground.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The unchastity of a woman shows in the upward glance of her eyes."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 26:12 "against-every-arrow she-will-open her-quiver" — the image
**Verse:** 26:12
**EMET:** "against-every-arrow she-will-open her-quiver"
**LOGOS:** "to every arrow she will open her quiver"
**PNEUMA:** "opens her quiver to every arrow"
**Issue:** The image is of sexual availability — the quiver opened to receive any arrow. The Greek is σαγίτταν — "arrow." All agents preserve the image, which the Greek text carries. The sexual metaphor is standard in ancient literature. SOPHIA retains it.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "and to every arrow she will open her quiver."

---

## Disagreement 006 — 26:14 "silent-wife / wife who keeps silence / quiet wife"
**Verse:** 26:14
**EMET:** "A-silent-wife is a-gift of-the-LORD"
**LOGOS:** "A wife who keeps silence is a gift from the LORD"
**PNEUMA:** "A quiet wife is a gift from God"
**Issue:** γυναικὸς σιωπώσης — "a silent/quiet wife." The participle implies active keeping of silence. LOGOS captures this best. PNEUMA's "quiet" is more behavioral and less about active restraint of speech. Also "God" vs "the LORD" — κύριος = LORD.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A wife who keeps silence is a gift from the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 26:15 "continent-soul / self-controlled soul"
**Verse:** 26:15
**EMET:** "a-continent-soul"
**LOGOS:** "a continent soul"
**PNEUMA:** "a self-controlled soul"
**Issue:** ψυχῆς ἐγκρατοῦς — "a self-controlled/continent soul." "Continent" is archaic but precise. "Self-controlled" is more accessible. SOPHIA uses "continent" as this is a technical virtue term worth preserving.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a continent soul."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 26:16 "highest heavens / heights of the Lord / high places"
**Verse:** 26:16
**EMET:** "Like the-sun when it-rises-up in-the-highest heavens"
**LOGOS:** "Like the sun rising on the heights of the Lord"
**PNEUMA:** "Like the sun coming up over the LORD's high places"
**Issue:** ὑψώματα κυρίου — "the heights/heights of the LORD." The Greek has a genitive: "the LORD's heights." EMET omits this genitive. LOGOS and PNEUMA both preserve it. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Like the sun rising in the heights of the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 26:17 "holy-lampstand / sacred lampstand"
**Verse:** 26:17
**EMET:** "the-holy-lampstand"
**LOGOS:** "the holy lampstand"
**PNEUMA:** "the sacred lampstand"
**Issue:** λυχνίαν τὴν ἁγίαν — "the holy lampstand." The reference is to the Temple menorah. "Holy" and "sacred" both work; "holy" is the standard liturgical term. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the sacred lampstand" — "sacred" slightly more vivid; both are defensible.

---

## Disagreement 010 — 26:18 "golden-pillars / pillars of gold"
**Verse:** 26:18
**EMET:** "Like golden-pillars upon silver-bases"
**LOGOS:** "Like golden pillars on silver bases"
**PNEUMA:** "Like gold columns on silver pedestals"
**Issue:** στῦλοι χρύσεοι — "golden pillars/columns." "Columns" vs "pillars" is stylistic. "Pedestals" (PNEUMA) for βάσεσιν — "bases/foundations" is more interpretive. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Like pillars of gold on silver bases."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 26:22 "hired-woman / hired woman" as "spit"
**Verse:** 26:22
**EMET:** "A-hired-woman is-regarded like spittle"
**LOGOS:** "A hired woman is considered like spit"
**PNEUMA:** "A hired woman is worth no more than a spit"
**Issue:** πόρνη — "prostitute/hired woman." The comparison is to ἐμπτύσματος — "spit/spittle." This is stark social commentary. All three translate honestly. "Spit" and "spittle" are both used; SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A hired woman is counted like spit."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 26:26 "loud-voiced wife" passage
**Verse:** 26:26
**EMET:** "A-loud-voiced-wife — like a trumpet it-is-heard in-every-noise"
**LOGOS:** "A loud-voiced woman is like a trumpet sounding at every noise"
**PNEUMA:** "A loud woman is like a trumpet blaring at every disturbance"
**Issue:** σαλπίγγι — "trumpet." All agents agree on the image. "Noise" vs "disturbance" for ἐπεγέρσει — "rousing/disturbance." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A loud-voiced woman is like a trumpet heard at every disturbance."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 26:28-29 textual status (bracketed)
**Verses:** 26:28-29
**EMET:** Brackets as possible insertions
**LOGOS:** Brackets
**PNEUMA:** Brackets
**Issue:** These verses are found in some Vaticanus traditions but appear to anticipate ch. 27's merchant theme. All agents correctly bracket them. Minor wording differences in the translation but substance identical.
**Resolution:** All agents: Bracket vv. 28-29 consistently.
